points.description: States that the compiler copies (inserts, places, substitutes, expands) the inline function's code/body at the place(s) in the program where the function is called, i.e. the call is replaced by a copy of the function code. Wording such as 'the function body is pasted in wherever it is used', 'the code is duplicated at each call site' or 'the call is replaced by the function's code' earns full marks. Answers that only say the function is 'inlined', 'expanded', 'made faster' or 'handled at compile time' without saying the function's code is copied into the calling place earn partial marks. Saying the compiler 'runs' or 'executes' the function at compile time, or that only one copy of the code exists, earns no marks.

levels.says: Says the compiler copies/inserts the function's code where it is called, but does not make clear that this copy is made at every place the function is called (e.g. only 'the code is copied into the program').
Only says the function is inlined/expanded, or that the call is replaced by the function body, without saying that the function's code is copied into the calling place.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying the compiler makes a copy of the inline function's code at each place where the function is called (the call is replaced by the code). Part marks where the copying idea is present but the 'at every call site' part is missing, or where the answer only says the function is inlined/expanded without mentioning that its code is copied. No marks for answers that only claim speed benefits, say the function is executed at compile time, or say a single copy of the code is kept.
